results.name: family_leeds_budget
results.reply: Within your £350k budget, five areas stand out: **Garforth East** (£305k) leads on overall score with strong safety and community; **Meanwood** (£329k) excels on environment and schools; **Chapel Allerton North** (£310k) and **Far Headingley & Weetwood** (£318k) offer the best amenities and health services; and **Primley Park & Wigton Moor** (£349k) sits right at your cap with a great park setting. Wetherby West and Moortown score well but sit slightly over budget. Want me to shortlist any of these or dig into a specific one?

results.name: commuter_manchester
results.reply: With commuter weighting (transport and housing emphasised), the top of the 15 km ring splits into two camps: central areas like **New Islington South & Bradford**, **Castlefield & Deansgate** and **Greengate & Blackfriars** score near-perfect on transport (97–98) but sit low on safety (15–30) and community; suburbs like **Sale Central**, **Timperley North** and **Cheadle Hulme** are safer, greener and better for schools, but cost more (median £430–500k) and are a longer ride in. If you want, I can narrow by a budget or by a minimum safety score.

results.name: retiree_devon
results.reply:
I've tuned the ranking for your priorities (safety weighted up, noise down). The standout areas across Devon are the Exmouth coastal villages — **Exmouth Brixington** and **Exmouth Withycombe Raleigh** — which combine top safety (87 and 74), high environment scores and excellent climate, at around £290–310k. **Tavistock** in the Dartmoor fringe is a good inland option (£250k, safety 70), while quieter **Exeter** suburbs like **Heavitree West** offer better amenities and transport links if you want to stay closer to the city.

The trade-off: the quietest coastal spots score lower on transport and day-to-day amenities — worth visiting if you'd rely on a car. Want me to pull up a closer look at any of these, or save a few to your shortlist?

results.name: safest_bristol
results.reply: The safest neighbourhoods near Bristol are mostly in the surrounding councils — **Downend North** (safety 81) and **Emersons Green** (74) in South Gloucestershire top the list. Within Bristol city itself, **Westbury-on-Trym** is the safest at 69, followed by Westbury Park (58) and Henleaze (60). The trade-off: the inner-city areas score well on safety but very poorly on housing affordability, while the southern suburbs are cheaper but weaker on schools and transport.

Withdean Woods and Mile Oak stand out for safety and environment, while Patcham West & Westdene offers the best housing affordability in the set. Want me to drill into any of these, or filter by a specific priority (e.g. safety, schools, quietness)?

results.name: young_professional_london

Want me to dig into any of these in more detail?

results.name: profile_postcode

Its real strengths are amenities and nightlife (91st percentile), transport and health services; its clear weakness is safety (5th percentile), driven by high burglary, theft and road-collision rates. Typical house price is about £218k, though based on few recent sales so treat it as an estimate.

The good air quality, seaside access and close rail/GP sit in sharp contrast to that safety picture.

The trade-off is clear: Clifton and Redland are greener, better-schooled and more affluent but the least affordable, whereas Bedminster is the cheapest and most affordable. If budget is tight, Bedminster's affordability is real but comes with the safety trade-off; if schools and community matter most, Clifton is the strongest of the three.

results.name: what_is_measured_schools
results.reply: The "schools & childcare" theme (id `education`) uses three scored indicators — good primary schools nearby (England only), good secondary schools nearby (England, Wales, Scotland), and choice of good schools (all four nations) — plus good nurseries nearby (all four nations). Two further indicators, primary results and secondary results, are shown as context rather than scored, and are England-only. School inspections are benchmarked within each nation because the nations use different inspection regimes.

results.name: off_topic
results.reply:
**Morning Shift**

She arrives before the light,
a small dark engine, purring,
knocking biscuits off the shelf
with the precision of a cat
who knows she'll get away with it.

Then the window ledge, the sun,
the slow blink that says *I own you now.*
You try to leave the room —
one paw, then both,
on the keyboard, on the page,
on the one clean square of rug.

By three she's found the spot
where the radiators hum
and curls into a question mark,
a comma, almost nothing —
just a warm weight
proof the morning's not yet done.
